title_en: Reply of the Supreme People's Court on Whether a Victim in a Product Infringement Case May File a Civil Lawsuit against the Trademark Owner of the Product as Defendant

articles.content_en:
Beijing Higher People's Court:

Your court's Request and Report on the Result of Handling the Issue of Establishing the Subject of Litigation in the Case of Jing Qilian, Zhang Xinrong, et al. v. General Motors Corporation, General Motors Overseas Corporation, and Others concerning Damages (Jing Gao Fa [2001] No. 271) has been received. Upon study, we consider that any enterprise or individual that places its name, title, trademark, or other identifiable mark on a product, indicating itself as the manufacturer of the product, shall fall within the definition of "product manufacturer" under Article 122 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China and "producer" under the Product Quality Law of the People's Republic of China. In this case, General Motors Corporation is the trademark owner of the vehicle involved in the accident. Based on the victims' prosecution and the actual circumstances of this case, it is not improper to name General Motors Corporation, General Motors Overseas Corporation, and General Motors do Brasil Ltda. as defendants in this case.

This is our reply.
